Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for 3 days of acute diarrhea (4–5/day) with mild abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting; no blood or mucus; patient drinking well; provided supportive care guidance and red-flag/safety advice.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea for ~3 days.
- Frequency/character: 4–5 bowel movements/day; consistency varies by time of day from watery to loose.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Mild abdominal pain.
  - One episode of vomiting.
  - Appetite loss.
  - Possible mild fever (“maybe a little bit”), not significant per patient.
  - No blood or mucus in stool.
- Hydration/nutrition: Able to drink plenty; eating less due to reduced appetite.
- Exposures/triggers:
  - No recent travel.
  - No suspicious/outside/“dodgy” food reported.
- Course: Persistent over 3 days; patient concerned as it has “kept up.”
- Medications tried for this episode: None for diarrhea or abdominal pain.
- Ambiguous statement: Patient said “Mostly it’s been dry and red” (context unclear; conflict/uncertainty noted).
- Systems review (pertinent negatives): No rectal bleeding; no mucus in stool.
  
Past Medical History:
- Asthma (current vs past unclear; patient states “had asthma…still have it”).
  - Medication: Patient reports using an inhaler named “Lexapro/Laxepro” (medication name unclear; dose/route/frequency not documented; conflict noted as Lexapro is typically an oral antidepressant, not an inhaler).

Social History:
- No recent travel.
- Other social details (tobacco, alcohol, drugs, occupation, living situation) not documented.

Family History:
- Father: Hypertension; died of bowel cancer at age 62 (~10 years ago).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- General (telehealth observation): Clinician noted the patient does not appear dehydrated.

Investigations:
- None performed during this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute diarrhea (3 days), mild symptoms, no red flags (no blood/mucus; drinking adequately; one vomit; possible low-grade fever; appears not dehydrated).
  - Supportive care:
    - Hydration: Encourage fluids; use oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte) to replace electrolytes.
    - Diet: “Soft”/easily digestible foods (e.g., crackers, toast, jam). Avoid milk/dairy, meat, eggs, and fish while symptomatic. Yogurt allowed as a probiotic. Advance to boiled/mashed vegetables as tolerated.
    - Reintroduction: After 48 hours without diarrhea, gradually reintroduce meat/eggs/fish.
  - Monitoring and safety:
    - If diarrhea persists beyond 1 week or if blood appears in stool: arrange stool testing for pathogens; antibiotics may be needed if indicated.
    - If stool frequency increases significantly and dehydration is suspected: seek urgent care/hospital. Note: Clinician gave two thresholds during visit (>8/day vs 6–8/day; conflict noted).
  - Medications: None prescribed today.
  - Follow-up: Return if symptoms worsen (increasing frequency, inability to keep fluids down, signs of dehydration), if blood/mucus appears, or if not improving within a week.

- Issue 2: Asthma (historical/current).
  - Medication clarification needed: Name/type of inhaler unclear (“Lexapro/Laxepro”); confirm actual asthma medications and dosing at next review.

General plan items:
- Patient advised that recommendations are summarized in the app notes for reference.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements:
  - Vitals, full physical exam.
  - Comprehensive medication list and reconciliation (including asthma regimen details and dosing).
  - Allergy confirmation documented as “No known allergies,” but cross-check at follow-up.
  - Detailed social history (tobacco, alcohol, drugs), travel/food exposure details, and sick contacts not fully explored.
  - Past surgical history and immunization status not documented.
● Internal conflicts:
  - Diarrhea frequency threshold for concern stated as “more than eight times/day” in one instance and “about six to eight times/day” in another (conflict noted).
  - Asthma medication named as “Lexapro/Laxepro”; Lexapro is typically escitalopram (oral), not an inhaler (conflict/clarification needed).
  - Statement “Mostly it’s been dry and red” is unclear; context not established.
● Transcript quality:
  - Generally understandable; a few unclear/inaudible segments and medication name uncertainty.
